## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO)

### Purpose & Scope
The purpose of this policy is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their **probationary period**.[1]

---

### ⏱️ PTO Accrual
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, on a **per-pay-period basis**:

| Years of Service | PTO Days Per Year |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days |
| 3–5 years | 20 days |
| 6–10 years | 25 days |
| 11+ years | 30 days |
[1]

---

### 🗓️ PTO Usage
PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval **at least two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

### 📦 Carryover and Maximum Balance
Employees may **carry over up to 40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual stops when this maximum balance is reached.[1]

---

### 💼 PTO at Separation
Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO, up to a **maximum of 80 hours**, at their **current rate of pay**.[1]

---

## 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
This policy is designed **to provide income protection for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.**[1]

---

### Scope / Eligibility
This policy **applies to all regular full-time employees who have completed 90 days of continuous employment.**[1]

---

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period.**[1]

---

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks per disability period.** Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

---

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation.**[1]

---

### Claim Process
Employees must **notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability. A completed claim form and supporting medical documentation must be submitted to the disability administrator **within 15 days.**[1]

---

> ⚠️ **Please note:** This information is based solely on HR policy documents and does not constitute legal advice. If you have specific questions about your situation, please contact your HR representative directly.

---

## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO)

### 🎯 Purpose & Scope
The purpose of this policy is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have **completed their probationary period**.[1]

---

### ⏱️ PTO Accrual
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, on a **per-pay-period basis**:

| Years of Service | PTO Accrual |
|-----------------|-------------|
| 0–2 years | 15 days per year |
| 3–5 years | 20 days per year |
| 6–10 years | 25 days per year |
| 11+ years | 30 days per year |[1]

---

### 🗓️ PTO Usage
PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

### 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance
Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual stops once that maximum is reached.[1]

---

### 💼 PTO at Separation
Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO, up to a maximum of **80 hours**, at their **current rate of pay**.[1]

---

There are **two PTO policies**, and which one applies to you depends on your **employment status** (full-time or part-time):

---

## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) *(Full-Time)*

**Policy 50010** establishes the PTO policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to **all regular full-time employees who have completed their probationary period.**[1]

- **PTO Accrual** is based on years of service:
  - 0–2 years: **15 days/year**
  - 3–5 years: **20 days/year**
  - 6–10 years: **25 days/year**
  - 11+ years: **30 days/year**[1]
- **Carryover:** Up to **40 hours** of unused PTO may be carried over to the following calendar year. The maximum PTO balance at any time is **240 hours**.[1]

---

## 📋 Policy 50020 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) – Part-Time

**Policy 50020** establishes the PTO policy for eligible part-time employees. It applies to **all regular part-time employees who work a minimum of 20 hours per week and have completed their probationary period.**[2]

Key highlights:
- **PTO Accrual** is on a pro-rated, per-hour-worked basis:
  - 0–2 years: **0.0385 hours per hour worked**
  - 3–5 years: **0.0577 hours per hour worked**
  - 6+ years: **0.0769 hours per hour worked**[2]
- **Carryover:** Up to **20 hours** of unused PTO may be carried over per calendar year.[2]

---

> 💡 **Which one applies to you?**
> - If you are a **regular full-time** employee who has completed your probationary period → **Policy 50010**
> - If you are a **regular part-time** employee (working at least 20 hrs/week) who has completed your probationary period → **Policy 50020**

If you're unsure of your employment classification or probationary status, please reach out to your HR representative for clarification.

Here is a detailed comparison of the full-time and part-time PTO policies:

---

# 🗓️ PTO Policy Comparison: Full-Time vs. Part-Time

---

## 📋 Policy Overview

| | **Full-Time** | **Part-Time** |
|---|---|---|
| **Policy Number** | Policy 50010 | Policy 50020 |
| **Policy Title** | Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) | Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) – Part-time |

---

## 👥 Scope & Eligibility

- **Full-Time:** This policy applies to all regular full-time employees who have completed their probationary period.[1]

- **Part-Time:** This policy applies to all regular part-time employees who work a minimum of 20 hours per week and have completed their probationary period.[2]

---

## ⏱️ PTO Accrual

- **Full-Time:** Full-time employees accrue PTO based on years of service:
  - **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
  - **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
  - **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
  - **11+ years:** 30 days per year

  PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees accrue PTO on a pro-rated basis calculated from their regularly scheduled hours. Accrual rates are:
  - **0–2 years:** 0.0385 hours per hour worked
  - **3–5 years:** 0.0577 hours per hour worked
  - **6+ years:** 0.0769 hours per hour worked[2]

---

## 📅 PTO Usage

- **Full-Time:** PTO may be used for vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose. Employees must request PTO through the designated time-off system. Requests for three or more consecutive days require supervisor approval at least two weeks in advance.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees must request PTO in accordance with their regular schedule. PTO is deducted in hourly increments. Requests must be submitted through the time-off system.[2]

---

## 🔄 Carryover

- **Full-Time:** Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. Maximum PTO balance at any time is **240 hours**. Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees may carry over up to **20 hours** of unused PTO per calendar year. Accrual stops when maximum balance is reached.[2]

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

- **Full-Time:** Employees who separate from employment in good standing will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Policy 50020 does not specify a PTO payout upon separation.

---

## 🔁 Eligibility Changes

Part-time employees who transition to full-time status will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy.[2]

---

## 📝 Key Takeaways

| Feature | Full-Time (Policy 50010) | Part-Time (Policy 50020) |
|---|---|---|
| **Accrual Method** | Days per year (fixed tiers) | Hours per hour worked (pro-rated) |
| **Max Accrual** | Up to 30 days/year | Pro-rated based on hours |
| **Carryover Limit** | 40 hours | 20 hours |
| **Max Balance** | 240 hours | Not specified |
| **PTO at Separation** | Up to 80 hours paid out | Not specified |
| **Minimum Hours** | N/A (full-time) | 20 hours/week |
| **Request Method** | Time-off system | Time-off system |

Full-time employees benefit from higher accrual rates, a larger carryover allowance, a defined maximum balance cap, and a separation payout provision — advantages that are not available (or are more limited) under the part-time policy.

## 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
This policy is designed **to provide income protection for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.**[1]

---

### Eligibility (Scope)
This policy **applies to all regular full-time employees who have completed 90 days of continuous employment.**[1]

---

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period.**[1]

---

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

---

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation.**[1]

---

### How to File a Claim
Employees must:
1. **Notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability.
2. Submit a **completed claim form and supporting medical documentation** to the disability administrator **within 15 days.**[1]

---

If you have additional questions about this policy or need further clarification, feel free to ask!

## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO)

### Purpose & Scope
The purpose of this policy is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their **probationary period**.[1]

---

### ⏱️ PTO Accrual
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, as follows:
- **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
- **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
- **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
- **11+ years:** 30 days per year

PTO accrues on a **per-pay-period basis**.[1]

---

### 🗓️ PTO Usage
PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

### 🔄 Carryover and Maximum Balance
Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**. Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1]

---

### 💼 PTO at Separation
Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO, up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

**Scope:** This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their probationary period.[1]

Full-time employees accrue PTO based on years of service:
- **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
- **3–5 years:** 20 days per year

**Scope:** This policy applies to all **regular part-time employees** who work a minimum of **20 hours per week** and have completed their probationary period.[2]

1. **Accrual Structure:** Full-time employees earn a fixed number of days per year (up to 30 days for 11+ years of service), while part-time employees earn PTO as a fraction of every hour worked on a pro-rated basis.[1]​[2]

### 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

#### Purpose
This policy is designed to **provide income protection for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.**[1]

#### Scope / Eligibility
This policy **applies to all regular full-time employees who have completed 90 days of continuous employment.**[1]

#### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period.**[1]

#### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

#### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation.**[1]

#### Claim Process
Employees must **notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability. A completed claim form and supporting medical documentation must be submitted to the disability administrator **within 15 days.**[1]

---

If you have further questions about this policy or need clarification on any of its provisions, feel free to ask!

# 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO)

## Purpose & Scope

The purpose of this policy is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their **probationary period**.[1]

---

## ⏱️ PTO Accrual

Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, on a **per-pay-period basis**, as follows:

| Years of Service | PTO Days Per Year |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days |
| 3–5 years | 20 days |
| 6–10 years | 25 days |
| 11+ years | 30 days |[1]

---

## 🗓️ PTO Usage

PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval **at least two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

## 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance

Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual stops once this maximum is reached.[1]

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO, up to a maximum of **80 hours**, at their **current rate of pay**.[1]

---

> 💡 **Note:** If you are a part-time employee, a separate policy (Policy 50020) governs your PTO accrual and usage. Feel free to ask if you'd like details on that policy as well!

---

## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) *(Full-Time)*

**Policy 50010** applies to **all regular full-time employees** who have completed their probationary period.[1]

**Key Highlights:**
- Full-time employees accrue PTO based on years of service:
  - **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
  - **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
  - **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
  - **11+ years:** 30 days per year
  - PTO accrues on a **per-pay-period basis**.[1]

---

## 📋 Policy 50020 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) – Part-Time

**Policy 50020** applies to **all regular part-time employees** who work a **minimum of 20 hours per week** and have completed their probationary period.[2]

**Key Highlights:**
- Part-time employees accrue PTO on a **pro-rated basis** calculated from their regularly scheduled hours:
  - **0–2 years:** 0.0385 hours per hour worked
  - **3–5 years:** 0.0577 hours per hour worked
  - **6+ years:** 0.0769 hours per hour worked[2]
- Part-time employees may **carry over up to 20 hours** of unused PTO per calendar year.[2]
- Part-time employees who **transition to full-time status** will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy.[2]

---

## 🔍 Which Policy Applies to You?

| Condition | Applicable Policy |
|---|---|
| Regular **full-time** employee, past probationary period | **Policy 50010** |
| Regular **part-time** employee (min. 20 hrs/week), past probationary period | **Policy 50020** |

Please check your employment classification to determine which policy applies. If you're unsure of your status, reach out to your HR department for clarification.

Here is a detailed side-by-side comparison of the full-time and part-time PTO policies:

---

# 🗓️ PTO Policy Comparison: Full-Time vs. Part-Time

---

## 📋 Policy Overview

| | **Full-Time** | **Part-Time** |
|---|---|---|
| **Policy Number** | Policy 50010 | Policy 50020 |
| **Title** | Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) | Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) – Part-Time |

---

## 👥 Scope & Eligibility

- **Full-Time:** This policy applies to all regular full-time employees who have completed their probationary period.[1]
- **Part-Time:** This policy applies to all regular part-time employees who work a minimum of 20 hours per week and have completed their probationary period.[2]

---

## 📈 PTO Accrual

- **Full-Time:** Full-time employees accrue PTO based on years of service:
  - **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
  - **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
  - **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
  - **11+ years:** 30 days per year

  PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees accrue PTO on a pro-rated basis calculated from their regularly scheduled hours. Accrual rates are:
  - **0–2 years:** 0.0385 hours per hour worked
  - **3–5 years:** 0.0577 hours per hour worked
  - **6+ years:** 0.0769 hours per hour worked[2]

> 📌 **Key Difference:** Full-time employees accrue a fixed number of days per year by tenure tier (up to 4 tiers including 11+ years), while part-time employees accrue on a per-hour-worked basis across 3 tiers (up to 6+ years).

---

## 🕐 PTO Usage

- **Full-Time:** PTO may be used for vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose. Employees must request PTO through the designated time-off system. Requests for three or more consecutive days require supervisor approval at least two weeks in advance.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees must request PTO in accordance with their regular schedule. PTO is deducted in hourly increments. Requests must be submitted through the time-off system.[2]

> 📌 **Key Difference:** Full-time employees have a broader defined set of approved uses (vacation, illness, personal time, etc.) and a specific advanced-approval rule for extended absences. Part-time PTO is deducted in hourly increments aligned with their schedule.

---

## 🔄 Carryover

- **Full-Time:** Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. Maximum PTO balance at any time is **240 hours**. Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees may carry over up to **20 hours** of unused PTO per calendar year. Accrual stops when maximum balance is reached.[2]

> 📌 **Key Difference:** Full-time employees can carry over twice as many hours (40 vs. 20), and have an explicit maximum balance cap of 240 hours.

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

- **Full-Time:** Employees who separate from employment in good standing will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Policy 50020 does **not** specify a PTO payout upon separation.

---

## 🔁 Eligibility Changes (Part-Time Only)

Part-time employees who transition to full-time status will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy (Policy 50010).[2]

---

|---|---|---|
| **Accrual Method** | Fixed days/year by tenure | Hours per hour worked |
| **Tenure Tiers** | 4 tiers (up to 11+ years) | 3 tiers (up to 6+ years) |
| **Max Accrual** | 30 days/year (11+ yrs) | 0.0769 hrs/hr worked (6+ yrs) |
| **Carryover Limit** | 40 hours | 20 hours |
| **Max Balance Cap** | 240 hours | Not specified |
| **PTO at Separation** | Up to 80 hours paid out | Not specified |
| **Advance Approval** | Required (3+ consecutive days, 2 weeks notice) | Not specified |
| **Deduction Unit** | Not specified | Hourly increments |

If you have further questions about either policy, feel free to ask!

### 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

**Purpose**

This policy is designed to provide **income protection** for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.[1]

---

**Eligibility (Scope)**

This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed **90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

---

**Benefit Amount**

Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

---

**Duration of Benefits**

Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

---

**Qualifying Conditions**

Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

---

**Claim Process**

Employees must:
1. **Notify their supervisor and Human Resources** within **three (3) business days** of the onset of disability.
2. Submit a completed **claim form and supporting medical documentation** to the disability administrator within **15 days**.[1]

---

If you have additional questions about this policy or need help understanding your eligibility, please don't hesitate to ask!

### 🎯 Purpose & Scope
The purpose of this policy is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to **all regular full-time employees** who have completed their probationary period.[1]

---

### ⏱️ PTO Accrual
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on years of service as follows:
- **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
- **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
- **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
- **11+ years:** 30 days per year

PTO accrues on a **per-pay-period basis**.[1]

---

### 🗓️ PTO Usage
PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the designated time-off system. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

### 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance
Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual stops when this maximum is reached.[1]

---

### 💼 PTO at Separation
Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

The policy that covers time away from work when you are temporarily unable to work is **Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability**. Here is a summary of its key provisions:

---

## 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
This policy is designed to provide **income protection** for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.[1]

---

### Eligibility (Scope)
This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed **90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

---

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

---

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

---

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

---

### Claim Process
Employees must:
1. **Notify their supervisor and Human Resources** within **three (3) business days** of the onset of disability.
2. Submit a **completed claim form and supporting medical documentation** to the disability administrator within **15 days**.[1]

---

If you have additional questions about this policy or need guidance on initiating a claim, please reach out to your HR department.
